goalbuddy_receipt_v1.summary: Made OXC for TSRX publicly launch-ready without publishing it: the GitHub Pages-shaped static artifact now has scoped URLs, canonical/Open Graph/Twitter metadata, sitemap, robots, public source/package links, a read-only snippet playground fallback, a 1200x630 social card, current evidence-linked performance copy, release notes, machine-readable npm/VSIX/site/social payloads, and exact approval-gated launch instructions. A manual-only pinned Pages workflow builds and runs the complete static browser proof before deploying through the protected github-pages environment. No package, repository, Marketplace item, site, or social post was published.

commands.evidence: 5/5 launch-build and benchmark-freshness contracts passed: 14 public pages, scoped URLs, canonical/social metadata, sitemap/robots, exact 1200x630 PNG, no internal logo gallery, and only latest retained benchmark links.

78/78 system-Chrome checks passed against a dumb loopback static server, including SPA navigation, search, accessibility in both themes, mobile layout, exact static capability contract, hidden native controls, read-only Try-in-playground snippet restoration, performance, and zero browser errors/4xx responses.

89/89 system-Chrome checks passed against the localhost-only native server, including real Oxlint diagnostics/tooltips/config/severity filters/type-aware mode, Oxfmt diff/apply, URL sharing, mobile control containment, accessibility, and zero browser errors/4xx responses.

commands.cmd: npm run docs:build && npm run docs:check
commands.evidence: Built 14 public pages and verified all 46 generated documentation files byte-for-byte against a disposable rebuild.

3/3 launch-contract tests passed: one package/repository identity, complete 11-package/eight-VSIX launch manifest, approval gates, manual-only Pages workflow, exact social payload, and clean npm pack dry-runs for runtime/oxlint/oxfmt.
60/60 native lint/format/config/type-aware/editor/Vite/Vite+ product regressions passed, including real loopback Vite dev/HMR.
23/23 package, non-fork boundary, legal, CSS, native-object, and VSIX artifact checks passed after rebuilding the editor bundle for the new metadata.
205 locked Rust shipping dependency licenses and 12 bundled VS Code dependency licenses verified deterministically.

evidence: Red-first tests exposed and retained four launch defects: the benchmark row callback mismatch, missing capability-schema ok flag, mobile hero overflow/native-control clipping, and static Try-in-playground waiting for a native editor. Each now has a passing regression contract.
The final static site is a pure artifact under docs/dist. Its demo-capabilities.json advertises static/read-only behavior, and no API server or native executable is present in the deployment tree.

The manual Pages workflow has no push trigger, requires the exact DEPLOY WEBSITE 0.1.0 input, pins every official action to an immutable commit, runs the complete static browser proof, and grants pages/id-token write only to the protected deployment job.

The launch manifest records all eight native npm packages before runtime/oxlint/oxfmt, all eight target VSIX identities, the exact website payload, one social string/image, and five independent approval classes.

The multi-lens DX review led to an install-first quick start with exact package and repository commands, removal of stale packaging/public-launch claims, explicit registry/Marketplace readback boundaries, and a machine-check that launch-facing performance links always name the latest retained reports.
Desktop and 390px mobile screenshots were visually inspected after the browser suite; the mobile artifact now renders at exactly 390px rather than the prior 630px overflow width.
deviations: The in-app browser runtime reported no available browser binding after the mandated bootstrap audit. The retained system-Chrome suite was available and passed the static and native matrices; visual screenshots were also inspected locally.

The Pages action pins were resolved from the official GitHub repositories on 2026-07-16. Deployment was deliberately not dispatched because it is an external write requiring exact approval and a public source commit.
The workspace has no Git metadata, so generated freshness, allowed-file inventory, actionlint, package dry-runs, and deterministic artifact checks replace Git diff/cleanliness claims.
remaining_blockers: T027 must run the complete fresh clean-room install, mixed-toolchain, Markless/editor, external-fingerprint, and performance oracle against the launch-ready state.
T999 must perform the final requirement-by-requirement completion audit.

Repository push/creation, hosted eight-runner candidate production, npm publication, Marketplace publication, Pages deployment, and social posting remain separate external actions requiring exact user approval.
